PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-29
52M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports that his home glucose readings have been running a little high and that he has struggled to keep up with regular exercise. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and large evening meals, which were discussed. Over the past few weeks he has noticed mild ankle swelling by evening, prompting a cardiac screen today. Family has observed alternating periods of elevated, high-energy mood with less need for sleep and periods of low mood, which he is open to exploring. He works as an accountant, mostly seated. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 128/80, HR 74, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 210 lb, BMI 31.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace ankle edema, improves with elevation.
Psych: cooperative, normal speech rate today, linear thought process.
Labs (prior week): A1c 7.1%, fasting glucose 138 mg/dL, Hgb 12.1 g/dL, BNP 42 pg/mL, lipid panel at goal.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications, A1c 7.1%. Start metformin 500 mg daily, titrate as tolerated. Reviewed glucose monitoring and foot care. Referred to a certified health educator for glucose management.
2. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron every other day. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
3. R/o CHF; BNP normal. Ankle swelling is mild, improves overnight, and fits long hours seated at his desk; no echocardiogram needed. Advised leg elevation in the evenings and short walking breaks at work.
4. Concern for bipolar disorder; referred to psychiatry. Provided referral and reviewed warning signs to seek earlier care.

Return in 3 months to review glucose control, sooner for worsening swelling.
